native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (copper/gold + amber + monument count) peaked in the 14th-13th century BCE (BCE 1400-1300, Old Bronze Age) at a value of 4.24 Z-units. All three components increased toward the peak: copper/gold was the dominant driver (+3.02 Z over 4 centuries, slope +0.76/c), followed by monument count (+1.55 Z, slope +0.39/c) and amber (+1.06 Z, slope +0.27/c). The increase was concentrated in the transition from BCE 1500 to BCE 1400.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded capital.csv (39 century bins, BCE 4300-500) with decimal=',' for European-format Z-scores. 2) Verified all Z-columns are unit-variance (mean≈0, std≈1), confirming they are comparable and summable. 3) Computed SummedSC = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument at each century. 4) Identified peak: BCE 1400 and 1300 (tied, SummedSC=4.2381, OBA group). 5) Quantified component trends over BCE 1800→1400 (4-century window) and BCE 2000→1400 (6-century window): all three components show positive net change and positive slope. 6) Cross-validated against time_series_data.csv raw century values (37 non-null points): identical peak confirmed. 7) Produced full 39-century table with peak rows marked.

sub_hypo.text: All three social-capital components increased toward the peak. Over BCE 1800–1400, copper/gold was the dominant driver (+3.02 Z, slope +0.76 Z per century), followed by monument count (+1.55 Z, slope +0.39 Z per century) and amber (+1.06 Z, slope +0.27 Z per century).
